calc.title: Survival projections under each treatment input
calc.lead: Enter one profile. The model projects overall survival under every treatment on the menu for the recorded BCLC stage, holding the profile, stage and site fixed. Outputs are model projections, not treatment effects.

table.short.local: Local data, Site {site}: n / deaths / at risk at {h} mo
table.note.rmst: RMST (restricted mean survival time) is the area under the projected curve from 0 to {h} months, in months. Rows follow unrounded RMST; no ranks are assigned.
table.note.within: ≤2: within 2 months of the highest RMST, judged on unrounded values (a difference just above 2 is shown with extra decimals). The exploratory 2-month threshold does not define clinical equivalence.
table.note.dagger: †: at Site {site} this treatment does not meet all local criteria (at least 30 patients, 10 deaths and 10 patients at risk at {h} months). Lack of local support does not mean the pooled model omitted that treatment; it indicates greater reliance on information borrowed across hospitals.
table.note.counts: Local counts describe the Site {site}, BCLC {stage} treatment cells of the development cohort (appendix table S20), not a risk table for this profile.
table.note.horizon: The 2-month tolerance remains exploratory, with different proportional implications across horizons.

details.intro: The treatment-ranking sequence (TRS) orders this profile's menu treatments by decreasing projected RMST. It is compared position by position with the pooled stage reference in table 3A.
details.pos_caption: RMSTs at each position of the two sequences (months)
details.caveat.m: “M ≤2 months is exploratory, not clinical equivalence” (Methods). “M measures reordering, not every between-treatment difference” (appendix S4.2).
details.caveat.ref: “Pooled ranking references remain descriptive because they were derived from the evaluation cohort” (Discussion).
details.caveat.model: The paper's agreement figures come from out-of-fold predictions; this calculator uses a full-cohort refit, so its orders can differ (appendix S4.3).
caveats.title: The paper's caveats
caveats.intro: Quoted from the unpublished draft manuscript; its figures are provisional. They apply to every projection on this page.
caveat.1.text: These are point projections without patient-specific confidence bands.
caveat.2.text: Individual eligibility restrictions were not applied; statistical support does not establish clinical feasibility.
caveat.3.text: Immunotherapy was excluded and feasibility was not assessed. Moreover, 39.05% of patients had a leading projection without full local support.
caveat.4.text: Clinical translation requires assessment of feasible options, independent validation of their prognostic estimates, and integration with efficacy and safety evidence, treatment burden, patient priorities, and local data support.
caveat.5.text: The exploratory 2-month threshold does not define clinical equivalence.
caveat.6.text: These development-informed analyses within one city do not establish performance of the unchanged pooled model elsewhere.
caveat.7.text: Eligibility requires separate assessment of liver reserve, portal hypertension, tumour anatomy, technical feasibility, contraindications, and patient goals. Statistical data support does not establish clinical suitability. The projections are observational treatment-associated estimates, not validated individual treatment effects …
caveat.8.text: Observational allocation is susceptible to confounding by indication, limited overlap, and unmeasured selection; prediction accuracy and resampling cannot resolve these biases.

footer.about: About HCC-CPDA: methods, limitations and model card
about.title: About HCC-CPDA
about.lead: HCC-CPDA (HCC Comparative Prognostic Decision Aid) is the analytic framework of an unpublished draft manuscript. This page summarises that draft; each number cites its table or figure, and none is recomputed.
about.provisional: The study results on this page are quoted from the unpublished draft and are provisional: they may change when the analysis is re-run. The model card describes this build.
about.what.p1: The draft developed HCC-CPDA “to examine whether individualised prognosis coexists with concentrated treatment rankings and whether ranking information relates to observed survival” (Summary). It is evaluated at two levels: patient-level received-treatment prognosis and stage-level treatment-ranking patterns (Introduction; appendix figure S1).
about.what.p2: It is an analytic framework evaluated retrospectively, not a validated decision tool. On its role in BCLC-guided deliberation the draft states: “Its integration into this process and effects on decision quality were not evaluated” (Discussion). It also states: “The study did not evaluate a clinical implementation; any future deployment would require input checks, defined users, and independent evaluation” (appendix table S31).
about.cohort.p1: 13,456 patients and 8,296 deaths (61.7%) from three hospitals in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, reported as Site 1, Site 2 and Site 3 with 4,947, 3,352 and 5,157 patients (table 1).
about.cohort.p2: The source database held 16,388 records. Sequential exclusions were age younger than 18 years (8), duplicated covariate–outcome profiles (2), missing BCLC stage (254), multiple recorded treatment modalities (2,617) and immunotherapy alone (51) (appendix S1).
about.cohort.p3: “Overall survival used recorded survival time and event status; the time origin, accrual period, and follow-up dates require source verification” (appendix S1).
about.inputs.p1: The pooled model uses 15 clinical predictors plus recorded BCLC stage, hospital and treatment (Methods; appendix table S3). The 15 predictors are:
about.inputs.p2: Hospital enters as Site 1, 2 or 3 (appendix table S3). Treatment is not entered by the user; the draft states: “We changed the treatment input while holding each patient’s clinical profile, stage, and hospital fixed” (Methods).
about.inputs.p3: Appendix table S3 gives the unit of tumour diameter, total bilirubin, AFP and creatinine only as “Source-data unit retained”, and appendix table S31 lists source units and the meanings of categorical codes as items to confirm. This calculator uses cm for tumour diameter, following the study’s data documentation, and assumes mg/dL for total bilirubin and creatinine and ng/mL for AFP; the calculator marks these three as assumed units. It codes male sex, multiple tumours and positive or present findings as 1, following the study’s data dictionary. These units and codings await confirmation against the source records.
about.inputs.p4: The draft imputed missing predictors (Methods). This calculator does not impute: all 15 predictors, the stage and the site are required.
about.model.p1: XGBoost accelerated failure time (AFT) with normal errors on log survival time and a configuration locked before the final pooled evaluation (Methods): distribution scale 1.0, maximum tree depth 4, learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, row and column subsampling 0.85, L2 regularisation 50, L1 regularisation 2 and 412 boosting rounds (appendix table S5).
about.model.p2: Missing predictors were handled with ten stochastic chained-equation imputations fitted within each training fold, and predictions were averaged across the ten imputation-specific models (Methods).
about.model.p3: The survival curve is 1 − Φ[(ln t − f(x,a))/1.0] for t > 0, with survival defined as 1 at t = 0; RMST is the area under this curve from 0 to the stage-specific horizon (appendix S2.3).
about.model.p4: Horizons are 84, 84, 36, 24 and 12 months for BCLC 0, A, B, C and D (Methods). A treatment entered a stage menu if its pooled cell had at least 30 patients, 10 deaths and 10 patients at risk at the horizon; the rule is statistical, not an eligibility criterion (Methods; appendix S2.2).
about.model.table_caption: Stage menus (appendix table S4) and pooled stage references (table 3A, group G1)
about.model.p5: The same thresholds assess local support within each site: 43 of 75 hospital–stage–candidate-treatment cells met all local thresholds (Results; appendix tables S2 and S20).
about.perf.p1: Received-treatment prognostic performance in the original three-repetition, five-fold out-of-fold analysis (table 2). “Predictions were evaluated only under the treatment received” (appendix S3.1).
about.perf.t2a_note: C-indices average three repetition-specific estimates and use all 13,456 patients; errors and calibration use 13,073 patients in 25 supported stage–received-treatment cells; parentheses give pointwise conditional 95% CIs. Lower IBS, RMST MAE and calibration error indicate smaller errors (table 2A notes).
about.perf.t2b_caption: Table 2B — within-hospital performance of the pooled site-aware model
about.perf.t2b_note: KM: training-fold Kaplan–Meier benchmark. These are internal out-of-fold results; error evaluation used 4,394, 2,804 and 4,125 patients at Sites 1–3 (table 2B notes).
about.perf.p2: Pooled, IBS was 0.1451 versus 0.1712 for KM and RMST MAE 12.47 versus 14.01 months (Results; appendix table S7A). The same-stage, different-treatment C-index ranged from 0.6381 to 0.8274 across hospital–stage cohorts (Results; appendix table S7D).
about.rank.p1: Overall, 68.57% of patients matched the pooled stage reference exactly, 27.60% differed with a maximum RMST mismatch M ≤2 months, and 3.83% had M >2 months; top-treatment agreement was 84.60% (Results; figure 2).
about.rank.p2: One or two tolerance groups covered ≥95% of every hospital–stage cohort (Results; table 3).
about.rank.p3: “The 2-month tolerance is exploratory”, and “Stages are categories, not a temporal trajectory” (figure 2 legend). The calculator shows the sequence, agreement and M for one profile in its collapsed ranking details; it does not assign tolerance groups.
about.excl.p1: “Leave-one-hospital-out models were fitted to two hospitals and evaluated at the third without hospital identity” (Methods).
about.excl.table_caption: Prognostic performance at each excluded hospital (figure 3; appendix table S23)
about.excl.p2: “At excluded Site 3, the overall C-index was 0.827, yet both absolute-error estimates exceeded KM” (Discussion). “Point estimates are shown; confidence intervals and paired error-difference tests were not reported” (figure 3 legend).
about.excl.p3: “Omitting hospital identity produces a different fitted model from the primary pooled site-aware model” (appendix S7.2). The calculator uses the site-aware model.
about.notc.h: What the model does not consider
about.notc.p1: “Macrovascular invasion was excluded because coding differed across hospitals; performance status was excluded and entirely missing at Site 3” (Methods). Immunotherapy alone and multiple recorded treatment modalities were excluded from the cohort (appendix S1), so neither can be projected.
about.notc.table_caption: Clinical domains considered by BCLC and their representation in HCC-CPDA (appendix table S6, abridged)
about.notc.r1.bclc: Imaging-defined size, number and distribution; vascular invasion and extrahepatic spread.
about.notc.r1.cpda: Diameter, binary multiplicity, nodal involvement and distant metastasis; stage included. Detailed distribution absent; macrovascular invasion excluded for inconsistent coding.
about.notc.r2.bclc: Compensated versus decompensated cirrhosis; ALBI and detailed ascites, bleeding or encephalopathy assessment.
about.notc.r2.cpda: Cirrhosis, Child-Pugh class, bilirubin, INR and creatinine. Albumin/ALBI and detailed decompensation or portal-hypertension measures not explicitly included.
about.notc.r3.bclc: Cancer-related symptoms and ECOG performance status, with clinical interpretation and complementary frailty assessment.
about.notc.r3.cpda: Performance status excluded from the common set; missing in 42.93% overall and all Site 3 patients. Frailty not included; stage provides only indirect information.
about.notc.r4.bclc: AFP refines prognosis and selected treatment pathways; additional biomarkers require sufficient validation.
about.notc.r4.cpda: AFP included; broader biological or molecular characterisation not included.
about.notc.r5.bclc: Transplant candidacy, technical feasibility, liver reserve, comorbidities and contraindications.
about.notc.r5.cpda: Some relevant tumour and liver variables included; comprehensive eligibility assessments absent. Hospital identifies context, and pooled/local support measures data availability; neither establishes suitability.
about.notc.r6.bclc: Goals, preferences, values and psychosocial circumstances considered through CUSE-informed multidisciplinary deliberation.
about.notc.r6.cpda: Not included in the survival model.
about.notc.p2: “Child-Pugh class and recorded BCLC stage may indirectly summarise omitted domains but cannot recover their detail” (appendix S2.4).
about.limit.1.text: Observational allocation is susceptible to confounding by indication, limited overlap, and unmeasured selection; prediction accuracy and resampling cannot resolve these biases. Unavailable treatment dates and sequences prevent establishing first-line care. Multimodality exclusion may select a distinctive population, and calendar-era changes were not assessed. Omitted performance status and macrovascular invasion limit clinical coverage.
about.limit.2.text: Demographic and socioeconomic fairness was not evaluated.
about.limit.3.text: Ranking concentration depends on predictors, model, menu, horizon, averaging, and tolerance. Original menu/horizon sensitivities used frozen predictions; expanded validation refitted models but did not reassess individual eligibility. Pooled ranking references remain descriptive because they were derived from the evaluation cohort; hospital-exclusion references were training-derived.
about.limit.4.text: Conditional performance intervals omit refitting and model-selection uncertainty. The separate fitted-cohort bootstrap examines refitting variation for original patients, not out-of-sample performance. Received-treatment comparisons condition on fixed predictions, groups, and horizons, omitting selection uncertainty. Paired hospital-exclusion performance-loss estimates remain unavailable.
about.limit.5.text: Ranking persistence provides an incomplete account of transportability. At excluded Site 3, the overall C-index was 0.827, yet both absolute-error estimates exceeded KM. Calibration and prediction errors therefore require evaluation alongside discrimination and ranking coverage.
about.limit.6.text: Hospital exclusion evaluated models refitted without hospital identity and with training-specific menus. These development-informed analyses within one city do not establish performance of the unchanged pooled model elsewhere.
about.limit.7.text: The study is a retrospective, development-informed evaluation within Kaohsiung.
about.limit.8.text: The model did not apply patient-specific feasibility filters and excluded immunotherapy; its TT category does not represent the full range of contemporary systemic options.
about.limit.9.text: Local statistical support describes the available data and does not establish treatment eligibility.
about.calc.h: How this calculator's model differs from the paper
about.calc.p1: The draft's individual projections are archived out-of-fold predictions: figure 1 averages three out-of-fold repetitions, each already averaging the ten imputation-specific models, and “No new model was fitted” (appendix S4.1).
about.calc.p2: Out-of-fold predictions exist only for cohort patients. For a new profile, this calculator uses the fitted-cohort ensemble defined in appendix S4.3, “ten imputation-specific models fitted to all 13,456 patients”, refitted for this build with the locked configuration of appendix table S5. The draft notes that this analysis “was separate from out-of-fold prognostic evaluation and the repeated-out-of-fold ranking summaries; its point rankings can therefore differ” (appendix S4.3).
about.calc.li1: Numbers from this calculator will not equal figure 1 or appendix table S10.
about.calc.li2: The draft's performance results describe the out-of-fold procedure, not this refit.
about.calc.li3: The draft states no seed for a fitted-cohort model; the seed used here is provisional and is listed in the model card.
about.calc.li4: All inputs are required, so no imputation is performed when projecting. Each curve is the mean of the ten per-model curves, and RMST is integrated with the trapezoid rule on a monthly grid.
about.calc.li5: The fitted-cohort bootstrap of appendix S4.3 is not computed; every projection is a point estimate.
about.card.intro: Read at runtime from the model manifest of this build.
about.card.unavailable: The model files are not available in this build, so the model card cannot be shown.
about.card.hash_note: Short hash: the first 12 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over the ten booster SHA-256 values, in manifest order, joined by line breaks.
card.verified: Imputer returns complete rows unchanged (verified at build)
card.value.seed_rule: imputation seed = deploy_seed + 37*m; AFT tree seed = imputation seed + 1
card.value.imputation: 10 stochastic IterativeImputer completions (cpda.imputation.FoldImputer); imputers are not exported
card.value.inference: all 15 predictors, BCLC stage and site required; no imputation at inference
about.privacy.p1: Projections are computed in your browser. Inputs are not sent to any server, not stored by this site and never placed in the page address, and the form asks the browser not to keep its entries (autocomplete off). The site sets no cookies, loads nothing from other websites and has no analytics or trackers.
about.privacy.p2: Only your language preference is kept, in this browser’s local storage. The web host receives requests only for the site’s own files and the model files, and logs visitor IP addresses as web hosts do. On a shared computer, use a private browsing window and close it afterwards: browsers can keep their own copies of open pages.
about.status.p1: Research prototype, preview build for review (v0.1.0-mvp), accompanying an unpublished draft manuscript. Not for clinical use. Not reviewed, registered or approved by any regulatory authority; its regulatory status has not been determined.
about.status.p2: Intended users: health professionals and researchers reviewing this unpublished study. The model describes adults with hepatocellular carcinoma (BCLC stage 0 to D) treated at the three study hospitals in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, with one of the eight recorded treatment categories. Research use only; not for clinical use and not for patients’ own use.
